provenance.description: Advisory scheduling experiment, never reusable test evidence or proof of the 300-second target. All 430 retained actual worker records are hashed. Linux/macOS use latest successful node phases. Windows selects the complete actual two-worker trial for the proposed two-worker resource regime; the newly added count-ten node falls back to its actual latest three-worker observation. No provisional or linearly scaled count-ten estimate remains. Runner differences and worker contention are confounded; this selection does not prove reducing concurrency improves time. The first three groups charge calls/teardowns plus one maximum observed cold fixture setup. The independent serial pair retains both complete setup/call/teardown charges. Failed newer phases retain prior observations and never supply acceptance evidence.

group_sources.cost_policy: Full setup/call/teardown per node; no shared setup normalization.
group_sources.hypothesis: Serializing these two independent proofs may reduce overlapping nested-worker contention; no causal speedup is established.

Linux.policy: Latest successful phases; failed newer phases retain prior observation

Darwin.policy: Latest successful phases; failed newer phases retain prior observation

Windows.policy: Actual two-worker trial; actual latest successful fallback for new nodes

provenance.collection_scope: All 2210 nodes have actual hosted observations on every platform. No provisional costs.
prediction_limitations: Changing worker count may change every node duration.
Different runner speeds, co-location and nested worker counts remain confounded.
Phase models exclude provisioning, startup, command overhead and cross-job launch skew.
All commands and exact coverage gates must freshly pass before submission.
